blocks.title: Methods to Secure Data exam shortcuts
items: Need confidentiality → ENCRYPTION
Use encryption when unauthorized readers must not understand the data.
Example: Full-disk encryption protects a stolen laptop.
Need to verify data has not changed → HASHING
Hashing is primarily an integrity control.
Example: Compare a downloaded file hash with the published value.
Need to display only part of sensitive data → MASKING
Masking hides portions while preserving recognizable format.
Example: Display only the last four digits of a card number.
Replace sensitive value with substitute → TOKENIZATION
The real value is stored separately from the token.
Example: A payment system stores a token instead of the card number.
Make code/data harder to understand → OBFUSCATION
Obfuscation increases difficulty but is not a substitute for encryption.
Example: Application code is intentionally made difficult to read.
Need location-based compliance → GEOGRAPHIC RESTRICTIONS
Restrict storage or access to approved regions.
Example: Customer data must remain inside one country.
Need least exposure → SEGMENTATION + PERMISSIONS
Separate sensitive data and tightly control who can reach it.
Example: Payroll systems sit in a restricted segment accessible only to HR.
blocks.example: Focus on what the scenario is protecting: confidentiality, integrity, access, location, or legal handling requirements.

questions.q: A company needs stolen laptop data to remain unreadable without a key. Which protection method is best?
questions.explanation: Encryption protects confidentiality by making data unreadable without the key.

questions.q: An administrator wants to verify that a downloaded file has not changed. Which method is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Hashing is commonly used to verify integrity.

questions.q: A customer service screen should show only the last four digits of a Social Security number. Which method best fits?
questions.explanation: Masking hides part of sensitive data while keeping a usable display format.

questions.q: A payment system stores a substitute value instead of the actual card number, with the real value kept separately. Which method is this?
questions.explanation: Tokenization replaces sensitive values with non-sensitive tokens.

questions.q: A developer makes application code intentionally difficult to understand but does not apply cryptographic protection. Which method is this?
questions.explanation: Obfuscation makes code or data harder to interpret but is not equivalent to encryption.

questions.q: A company must ensure customer data is stored only within one approved country. Which method is most direct?
questions.explanation: Geographic restrictions constrain where data may reside or be accessed.

questions.q: Payroll systems are placed in a separate restricted network segment accessible only to HR. Which two methods are being combined?
questions.explanation: Segmentation separates the systems, while permission restrictions limit who can access them.
